In [[geometry]] and [[topology]], given a [[Group (mathematics)|group]] ''G'' (which may be a topological or Lie group), an '''equivariant bundle''' is a [[fiber bundle]] <math>\pi\colon E\to B</math> such that the total space <math>E</math> and the base space <math>B</math> are both [[Lie group action|''G''-space]]s (continuous or smooth, depending on the setting) and the projection map <math>\pi</math> between them is equivariant: <math>\pi \circ g = g \circ \pi</math> with some extra requirement depending on a typical fiber.

For example, an [[equivariant vector bundle]] is an equivariant bundle such that the action of ''G'' restricts to a linear isomorphism between fibres.

== References ==
*Berline, Nicole; Getzler, E.; Vergne, Michèle (2004), Heat Kernels and Dirac Operators, Berlin, New York: Springer-Verlag
